newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mostly higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended a quiet afternoon mostly firmer as attention shifted to Friday's October U.S. jobs data.
Brisk morning trade wound down quickly after Europe closed, and although daily volume was moderate, prices drifted in spotty trade during the latter portion of the session.
Volume was estimated on the price boards at about 25,000 marks, 18,000 Swiss francs, 24,000 yen and 15,000 sterling, floor brokers said.
Currencies found little incentive from the Federal Reserve's Beige Book of economic activity.
December sterling returned toward its new contract high at $1.6334 late in the session, still underpinned by the rise in U.K. interest rates that had caught some traders off-guard by its timing.
The Bank of England on Wednesday raised its minimum lending rate 25 basis points to 6.0 percent.

At the same time, marks and Swiss francs each had backed down from resistance levels, at about $0.6667-70 and $0.8052-55, respectively, although the Swiss unit's pullback occurred on especially scanty volume and lacked force, floor brokers said.

Yen regained some ground lost recently on the mark cross and although Canadian dollar cut gains, it stayed buoyant enough to persuade some traders that players are still holding onto short yen/long Canada spreads in the expectation that the Canadian unit has more upside.

Indeed, Goldman Sachs' foreign exchange economist Jim O'Neill said on Wednesday that the Canadian currency is probably "the best place to be" out of the Canadian, New Zealand and Australian currencies.
Currencies had muted response to the rise and fall in U.S. Treasury bond futures or to the Federal Reserve's Beige Book.

The Fed said the pace of U.S. growth has slowed somewhat but wage pressures remain, manufacturing is stable to stronger and consumer spending moderate. It said most districts described labor markets as tight and that construction activity was strong in some areas, slackening in a few.
Brokers said the report did not reveal enough new insights into the economy to jar the market much.

Dec yen rose $0.000024 to $0.008830, marks eased $0.0005 to $0.6639, Swiss fr up $0.0002 at $0.8006, pound rose $0.0230 to $1.6322, Canadian dollar added $0.0014 to $0.7470, Aussie dollar up $0.0009 at $0.7905, Mex peso fell $0.001000 to $0.120650. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
